selection_rule: REVISED 2026-08-18 after N-54. Three geometric GATES first, then wind exposure x separation dilution over 449 real KIAD observations. Gates: (B) true edge-to-edge gap > intake standoff + radius = 50 m, so the intake disc sits in free air and not inside the source hall; (C) the source LONGEST facade must FACE the receptor, so a realistic condenser bank has a straight plume path -- the original version skipped this and picked a pair where N-54 measured 100 % of downwind bearings REFUSED; (D) longest facade >= 100 m. NOT chosen by floor area.

gates.derivation_of_min_gap: INTAKE_STANDOFF_M + INTAKE_RADIUS_M, imported from build_site so the two files cannot drift

convention: wind FROM X means air moves toward X+180. Receptor at bearing B from source is exposed when the wind comes FROM (B+180) mod 360.

assumptions_not_in_osm: Building HEIGHT is absent from OSM for these footprints, so the solver's building height remains a stated assumption rather than a measurement.
Condenser bank POSITION is not mapped anywhere. It is placed on the source face pointing at the receptor, which is the physically conservative worst case.
Intake POSITION is likewise assumed, on the receptor face pointing at the source.
attribution: Building footprints (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. Weather: NOAA ASOS via Iowa State Environmental Mesonet. No FortyGuard credential used.
selected_by: commit_site.py -- three stages: (1) select_site.py geometric gates, (2) refusal_rank.py MEASURED usable exposure, (3) architecture SCOPE GATE from architecture_verdicts.json, which has VETO power over the ranking. Chosen: rank 1 on physics, and the highest-ranked candidate assessed as GRADE-cooled and therefore inside PLAN section 8d's scope.

superseded_selection.why: ranked top on exposure x dilution but MEASURES 100 % of downwind bearings refused; path clearance was only +0.144, i.e. the long facade is nearly perpendicular to the receptor. A boolean clearance gate cannot detect this.

architecture_gate.evidence: ESRI frame, annotated with both OSM footprints (annotate_screen.py). BOTH roofs are plain white/grey with only small scattered penetrations -- no equipment arrays on either roof. The SOURCE carries a double row of ~20 uniform rectangular units in a strip along its north facade, outside the roof line, at grade. The RECEPTOR encloses a 4x6 grid of large rectangular units plus 3-4 white vertical cylindrical tanks in a yard -- a central plant with chillers or dry coolers and water/thermal storage, at ground level.

vetoed_higher_ranked.name: Digital Realty Northern Virginia IAD35 -> IAD36
vetoed_higher_ranked.why: Fails PLAN section 8d. Excluded despite ranking FIRST on measured usable exposure (0.3172, 0.0 % refused). Selecting purely for plume-path physics would have committed the project to a site whose scope premise is false.

vetoed_higher_ranked.name: Vantage Santa Clara CA2 -> 1075445245
vetoed_higher_ranked.why: Fails PLAN section 8d and is EXCLUDED, despite santaclara having the best numbers of any new metro: the densest OSM cluster outside Ashburn (53 tagged data centres), the highest wind exposure (53.1 %), and 99.88 % weather coverage. No FortyGuard call was bought for it. Six further annotated frames remain to be screened for a grade-cooled pair.

vetoed_higher_ranked.name: unnamed tagged data centres, Mesa AZ
vetoed_higher_ranked.why: EXCLUDED. Recirculation between two buildings cannot be modelled when neither exists. No FortyGuard call was bought. The other Arizona cluster (Chandler: CyrusOne, Digital Realty, H5; 10 tagged; KPHX at 20.6 km) has not been screened yet.

architecture_gate.resolution_caveat: ESRI World Imagery and USGS National Map are ~0.3-0.5 m. At that scale we see OBJECTS, not nameplates. We cannot certify whether a unit is a chiller, a condenser, an air handler or a fan, and we cannot measure heights. The grade-vs-roof distinction is what is claimed, nothing finer.
